bill.title: Keeping All Students Safe Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.

industries.rationale: The bill directly regulates schools and Head Start programs, imposing new training requirements, compliance procedures, and enforcement obligations on educational institutions.
The bill creates a new private right of action for students subjected to unlawful seclusion or restraint, which would generate litigation opportunities.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prohibit schools and Head Start programs that receive federal funding from using seclusion (confining a student alone in a locked room) and would restrict the use of physical restraints to situations where a student poses an imminent danger of serious physical injury. It requires staff training in crisis intervention, establishes procedures for reporting incidents, and creates enforcement mechanisms including the ability for students to sue and for federal agencies to withhold payments from programs that violate the rules. The bill also provides grants to help state education agencies implement these policies.

plain.whoItTouches: Students, teachers, and the families paying for it.

bill.title: A joint resolution proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States relating to contributions and expenditures intended to affect elections.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: Organizations that spend money to influence elections would face new potential restrictions on their expenditures and fundraising.
The amendment would create new constitutional authority to regulate campaign finance, directly affecting election law practice and lobbying activity.
Limits on campaign spending could affect demand for political advertising across broadcast, digital, and print media platforms.
The amendment's authorization to distinguish between natural persons and corporations could affect how financial institutions participate in election-related spending.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment that would allow Congress and state governments to set limits on how much money candidates and others can raise and spend to influence elections. It would also permit lawmakers to treat corporations and other legal entities differently from individual people, including by prohibiting those entities from spending money on elections. The amendment would require ratification by three-fourths of the states to take effect.

bill.title: A joint resolution terminating the national emergency declared with respect to energy.
bill.latestActionText: Failed of passage in Senate by Yea-Nay Vote. 47 - 51. Record Vote Number: 554.

industries.rationale: The emergency declaration explicitly expedites approvals for oil, gas, and coal development and infrastructure, which this resolution would terminate.
The emergency order covers renewable energy resources and infrastructure, so ending it would affect expedited permitting for solar, wind, and storage projects.
The emergency declaration addresses energy infrastructure and supply adequacy, directly affecting utilities' ability to build transmission and generation facilities under expedited timelines.
The emergency order includes critical minerals and uranium in its definition of energy resources subject to expedited development.
The emergency invokes military construction authority and expedites energy infrastructure projects, affecting contractors who build pipelines, power plants, and related facilities.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would end the national energy emergency that the President declared in January 2025. That emergency declaration directed federal agencies to speed up approvals for energy projects—including oil, gas, coal, renewables, and infrastructure like pipelines—and gave the Defense Department authority to use emergency construction powers to address energy supply vulnerabilities. Terminating the emergency would remove those expedited authorities and return permitting and development processes to their standard procedures.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who buys fuel or heats a home. People who live near a mine, and people who work in one.

industries.rationale: The emergency declaration explicitly directs expedited approval of oil, gas, and coal development and infrastructure; terminating it would remove those fast-track authorities.
The emergency order covers renewable resources and energy storage; ending it would affect expedited permitting for solar, wind, and grid projects.
The emergency declaration includes critical minerals and uranium extraction; termination would remove expedited development authorities for these materials.
The emergency order addresses energy infrastructure and supply adequacy; utilities would lose access to expedited permitting for transmission and generation projects.
The emergency invokes military construction authority and expedited infrastructure completion; terminating it would affect contractors working on energy-related projects.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would end the national energy emergency that the President declared in January 2025. That emergency declaration directed federal agencies to speed up approvals for energy projects—including oil, gas, coal, renewables, and infrastructure like pipelines—and gave the Defense Department authority to use emergency construction powers to address energy supply vulnerabilities. Terminating the emergency would remove those expedited authorities and return permitting and development processes to their standard procedures.

DESCRIPTION:THIS AGREEMENT PROVIDES FUNDING UNDER THE INFLATION REDUCTION ACT (IRA) TO CLIMATE UNITED (CU). THE RECIPIENT WILL UTILIZE THE FUNDING TO REDUCE EMISSIONS OF GREENHOUSE GASES AND OTHER AIR POLLUTANTS; DELIVER BENEFITS OF GREENHOUSE GAS- AND AIR POLLUTION-REDUCING PROJECTS TO AMERICAN COMMUNITIES, PARTICULARLY LOW-INCOME AND DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES; AND MOBILIZE FINANCING AND PRIVATE CAPITAL TO STIMULATE ADDITIONAL DEPLOYMENT OF GREENHOUSE GAS- AND AIR POLLUTION-REDUCING PROJECTS.

SPECIFICALLY, THE RECIPIENT WILL ENDEAVOR TO ACCOMPLISH THIS BY WORKING WITH COMMUNITY GROUPS, TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROVIDERS, FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS, AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT ENTITIES TO REDUCE THE BARRIERS AND LIMIT THE INEFFICIENCIES THAT HAVE PREVENTED BROAD ADOPTION AND FINANCING OF CLEAN TECHNOLOGIES. TO ENSURE CLEAN ENERGY ACCELERATION AND MARKET TRANSFORMATION BEYOND THE NATIONAL CLEAN INVESTMENT FUND (NCIF), CLIMATE UNITED WILL INTEGRATE THIS CAPITAL RESOURCE INTO EXISTING LENDING PRODUCTS AND PROCESSES SO THAT ALL LENDERS, (I.E., BEYOND JUST THE COMMUNITY, GREEN AND NONPROFIT SECTORS) LEARN TO ADDRESS DECARBONIZATION IN THEIR ROUTINE LENDING PRACTICES. GREENING EXISTING LENDING WITH NCIF SUPPORT WILL HAVE THE BROADEST TRANSFORMATIVE IMPACT ON THE CAPITAL MARKETS NATIONWIDE.
ACTIVITIES:THE ACTIVITIES INCLUDE DEVELOPING A SUSTAINABLE FUND THAT CAN BE REVOLVED WHILE OFFERING PRODUCTS THAT MEET BORROWERS AND MARKETS WHERE THEY ARE.  SPECIFICALLY, THEY INTEND TO LEVERAGE EPA FUNDS WITH PRIVATE CAPITAL TO PROVIDE ADEQUATE LEVELS OF SUBSIDY TO SPUR THE ADOPTION OF GREEN ALTERNATIVES. AS COSTS COME DOWN AND MARKETS MATURE, THEY PLAN TO SLOWLY DECREASE THE AMOUNT OF SUBSIDY PER TRANSACTION TO ENSURE THEIR PRODUCTS ARE ADDITIVE AND TO MAXIMIZE SUSTAINABILITY OF THE FUND. CLIMATE UNITED'S PLAN IS TO BUILD A SUPPORTIVE ECOSYSTEM FOR THE FINANCING OF QUALIFIED PROJECTS (QP) THAT LEVERAGE NATIONAL NETWORKS OF LOCAL IMPLEMENTATION PARTNERS AND COORDINATION WITH LABOR AND WORKFORCE ORGANIZATIONS TO ENSURE FINANCED PROJECTS ARE (I) GENERATING HIGH-QUALITY JOBS WITH A DIVERSE, SKILLED WORKFORCE TRAINED IN DBRA COMPLIANCE AND REPORTING WHERE APPLICABLE, (II) DELIVERING HIGH-PERFORMING BUILDINGS FOR OWNERS AND OCCUPANTS OR ACCESS TO CLEAN ENERGY OR TRANSPORTATION FOR AMERICAN FAMILIES, BUSINESSES, AND ORGANIZATIONS, AND (III) ELIMINATING THE BARRIERS THAT HAVE HISTORICALLY PREVENTED THE SCALING OF CLEAN ENERGY TECHNOLOGIES ACROSS SEGMENTS. 

THEIR CAPITAL DEMAND SIDE MARKET-BUILDING PLAN FOCUSES ON BROAD AWARENESS BUILDING, TARGETED OUTREACH AND EDUCATION, AND STRAIGHTFORWARD CONVERSION TO ADDRESS HISTORIC BARRIERS. THE FOUNDATION OF THEIR STRATEGY WILL BE POTENTIAL PARTNERSHIPS WITH NATIONAL NETWORKS OF LOCAL ORGANIZATIONS THAT WILL ENGAGE, EDUCATE, AND EQUIP LOCAL PARTNERS WITH THE TOOLS TO FACILITATE QP DEVELOPMENT. CLIMATE UNITED WILL DEVELOP OR PARTNER TO DELIVER ONGOING TRAINING TO LENDERS, CONTRACTORS, OWNERS, COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS, BUILDING OPERATORS, AND OTHER PRIORITY SEGMENTS, IN CONJUNCTION WITH ESTABLISHED, ON THE GROUND COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS. THEY WILL WORK WITH CCIA PARTNERS CREATING TRAINING PROGRAMS TO PROVIDE THE MOST UP-TO-DATE INFORMATION ON THEIR PRODUCTS AND PROCESSES TO BUILD THE CONTINUATION OF SUPPORT FOR COMMUNITY LENDERS AND BUILD TRAINING FOR COMMUNITY BASED ORGANIZATIONS AROUND HOW TO ACCESS CLIMATE UNITED FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE.

THEIR CAPITAL SUPPLY SIDE MARKET-BUILDING PLAN FOCUSES ON ASSET AND DATA STANDARDIZATION, FINANCIAL PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT, PORTFOLIO ANALYSIS, AND MARKET EDUCATION. THROUGH A COOPERATIVE DESIGN PROCESS WITH TRANSACTION PARTNERS, THEY WILL CREATE AND REFINE THEIR STANDARDIZED PRODUCTS SO THEY CAN MORE QUICKLY SCALE AND SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF VIABLE SECONDARY MARKETS.SUBRECIPIENT:A PORTION WILL BE DEPLOYED TO BALANCE SHEETS INVESTING IN AND WITH TRANSACTION PARTNERS TO FACILITATE STANDARDIZED AND TAILORED LOANS INTO QPS THAT MAY STAY ON THE BALANCE SHEETS OF THE COMMUNIT

DESCRIPTION:THIS AGREEMENT PROVIDES FUNDING UNDER THE INFLATION REDUCTION ACT (IRA) TO POWER FORWARD COMMUNITIES (PFC). THE RECIPIENT WILL UTILIZE THE FUNDING TO REDUCE EMISSIONS OF GREENHOUSE GASES AND OTHER AIR POLLUTANTS; DELIVER BENEFITS OF GREENHOUSE GAS- AND AIR POLLUTION-REDUCING PROJECTS TO AMERICAN COMMUNITIES, PARTICULARLY LOW-INCOME AND DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES (LIDACS); AND MOBILIZE FINANCING AND PRIVATE CAPITAL TO STIMULATE ADDITIONAL DEPLOYMENT OF GREENHOUSE GAS- AND AIR POLLUTION-REDUCING PROJECTS.

SPECIFICALLY, THE RECIPIENT -- FORMED BY FIVE OF THE COUNTRY'S MOST TRUSTED HOUSING, CLIMATE, AND COMMUNITY INVESTMENT GROUPS -- WILL BUILD AND LEAD A NATIONAL FINANCING PROGRAM TO PROVIDE CUSTOMIZED AND AFFORDABLE CAPITAL SOLUTIONS FOR SINGLE-FAMILY AND MULTI-FAMILY HOUSING OWNERS AND DEVELOPERS, DRIVING DOWN COSTS AND CREATING STRONGER, MORE AFFORDABLE, MORE RESILIENT HOMES. THE COALITION WILL ALSO DEDICATE TIME AND FUNDING TOWARDS COLLABORATING WITH AND EDUCATING COMMUNITY MEMBERS TO HELP PRIORITIZE THE BEST SOLUTIONS FOR AN INDIVIDUAL'S SPECIFIC NEEDS IN AN EFFORT TO PROVIDE LASTING AND GENUINELY-IMPACTFUL SOLUTIONS.
ACTIVITIES:THE ACTIVITIES INCLUDE A BALANCE OF LOCAL IMPLEMENTATION WITH A NATIONAL STRATEGY TO DELIVER FOCUSED, SCALED, AND LIDAC-FIRST MARKET TRANSFORMATION. POWER FORWARD COMMUNITIES (PFC) WILL ENRICH THE LOCAL IMPLEMENTATION, LED BY COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS (CBOS), BY PUTTING ALL BUILDING OWNERS IN A POSITION TO ACT THROUGH AWARENESS CAMPAIGNS AND EXPANDING ACCESS TO INDIVIDUALIZED, ACTIONABLE INFORMATION INCLUDING PLANNING TOOLS, SIMPLIFIED CHOICES, AND TRUSTWORTHY AND RELIABLE SUPPORT SERVICES, IN ADDITION TO SUPPORTING A VETTED LOCAL CONTRACTOR NETWORK. THE NATIONAL STRATEGY WILL WORK TO REDUCE THE COST OF PARTICIPATION AND STREAMLINE PROJECT DELIVERY AND REDUCE FRICTION, ALONGSIDE CUSTOMIZED AND AFFORDABLE FINANCING SOLUTIONS. ADDITIONALLY, PFC WILL MOBILIZE A VARIETY OF AFFORDABLE CAPITAL SOLUTIONS THAT CATER TO A VARIETY OF PROJECTS AND NEEDS.
